name: Wet Asphalt
desc: A rain-soaked road running out to a hazed horizon — chip-seal aggregate, tar-seam snakes and a palimpsest of patches under converging lane paint — where the water film takes unseen streetlights and neon and smears them into long wobbling columns of reflection, rain dimples the surface into dying rings, and the tarmac at your feet turns to a mirror.

energy.doc: how hard the reflections burn, how long the columns smear, and the rain

scale.doc: perspective spread of the road plus aggregate and reflection width

density.doc: how many unseen light sources are reflected, plus rain and aggregate

wear.doc: tar seams, patches and worn-out lane paint

speed.doc: scroll rate of the road and the ripple on the water

hue.doc: primary reflected-light hue (28 = sodium amber; the road itself sits cold on the complement)

y.doc: horizon line y — nothing is ever painted above it

alpha.doc: opacity of reflections, rain and sheen

style.doc: slick: mirror-wet night road, saturated light columns wobbling the full depth of the frame · drizzle: only damp — the surface goes matte, the reflections diffuse away and the road reads grey, flat and cold · oil: a thin-film slick floating on the water, spilling interference rainbows across the ruts — colour as chemistry, not lighting · sodium: a single old sodium-vapour hue over everything, near-monochrome amber with everything else crushed to black

act.doc: drift: steady travel down the road · haul: the road lurches forward on every kick · idle: nearly stopped, rain off, the reflections just breathing

seed.doc: deterministic seed for aggregate, patches, tar seams and where the lights sit
